parts.text: Which claim correctly counts those lines?

options.text: Two: the fold through the midpoints of each pair of opposite sides, and each passes the fold test.
Infinitely many, because any line through the centre looks balanced at a glance.
The count needs group-theory language before any fold can be checked.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: The diagram shows Gopal's rectangular card. Opposite sides are equal and all angles are $90^\circ$, but adjacent sides are unequal. He wants to count its lines of symmetry by testing folds.

part_answers.answer: A non-square rectangle has exactly two lines of symmetry: the two mid-lines joining midpoints of opposite sides; diagonal folds do not match unequal adjacent sides.

teacher.key_rationale: A non-square rectangle has exactly two reflection lines (mid-lines of opposite sides). Infinite lines omit the fold test. Group-theory language is out of scope.
teacher.figure_note: Rectangle with two dashed mid-line fold candidates.
